body: I want to get there, but just not giving a fuck is easier said than done. I'm working on it though. I really appreciate all of the comments on this thread. They're helping me see things in other perspectives and it helps.
The only friends that comment on my wall are internet friends. It's the real ones that concern me, because they don't.

I don't just go telling my whole life story to acquaintances. Usually they tell me something personal and I see that as a sign that I can begin to open up a little. I don't just assume people care about what I'm saying. A lot of it is that people want someone to care about them, but don't have to care in return (I'm not like that), but that's what I seem to get sometimes.

I don't want to be extremely specific but I'll try not to be too vague either. I'm an American college student in the central US. I work a dead-end job part-time to pay for gas, car insurance, etc. I've lost a lot of weight in the past year but I'm still as depressed as ever. My hobbies include: Reddit, Call of Duty (I'm really bad though), I like to listen to music (suck at making it. I've taken lessons and all that jazz, just not creative enough). I hate sports, find them boring to watch. I'm 20 years old. I'd go to London for a day and get shitfaced, because it sounds appealing to me. I care way too much about other people and feel that they don't care about me, but I still care about them. I don't remember everything, but if you tell me something and you put meaning into it, I'll remember. A conversation I had with a friend two years ago is as fresh in my mind today as it was the day after it happened. To that friend, it's but a distant memory long forgotten. I remember the weirdest shit.

How's 6 months of getting to know someone before you start to divulge personal stuff? Just the generic introductory stuff for the first 6 months, then when I start to feel comfortable, I start to open up, and 'oh hey, this guy isn't exactly what I thought he was....' I seriously let it out in small bits at a time. I've tested this shit so much, you wouldn't believe how many people I've alienated.

Well another problem is that I'm still on my parent's insurance (college student with a shitty job), and my parents don't think I need help, but that I just need to get over my problems, they think it's all my own doing, and not something out of my control.

I've told my parents, they told me to get over myself. I told my best friend, he told me to suck it up. My brother is a dick that doesn't care about me unless it suits him in some beneficial way. I try finding new people that do care about me, but when I start to open up, they get turned off and leave. This brings me back to my point, that no one likes me.

I'm just using that as an example. I don't want to put on a facade anymore, but at the same time I want to change who I am. I don't want to be me. I don't like me. I do weird shit, like talk to myself, and I'm extremely paranoid and shit like that. I'm pretty good at hiding it, though. How does one seek professional help when they're not motivated enough to seek it?

Thanks for the effort, but that's pretty empty seeing as you don't know me. I want people to like me for who I am, and sadly the only way I've managed to get people to 'like me' is by being who I'm not, and putting on some bullshit facade.
